test.title: The town that moved its station

paragraphs.text: For sixty years the railway station of Alderby stood a mile outside the town. Passengers arriving in the evening had to walk along an unlit road, and shopkeepers complained that visitors rarely reached the market square.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: In 2012 the council began a campaign to move the station closer to the centre. The railway company refused at first, saying that a new platform would slow down freight trains that passed through at night.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A compromise was found in 2016: the old station was kept for freight, and a small passenger halt was built beside the square. Since then, the number of visitors staying for a meal has risen sharply.
paragraphs.label: C
